paragraphs: CourtCall sells a remote appearance service that lets attorneys and other participants take part in court proceedings without traveling to the courthouse. The company says its platform can meet the remote collaboration needs of a court, law firm, administrative agency or corrections facility.

Appearances run over video, audio or telephone. Attorneys use it to appear for routine matters in civil, family, criminal, probate and bankruptcy cases. Participants schedule, continue or cancel an appearance before the hearing. Before doing so, the site asks users to check its list of participating courts.

CourtCall states that it was established in 1995 to make remote court appearances simple, accessible and affordable for all parties. It describes providing supported remote legal collaboration services throughout the United States, Canada and worldwide. A home page announcement says the company was the successful bidder on the Colorado Judicial Department solicitation RFP #25005 and entered into an agreement with the department.
